inputs.original_text: I just heard about this case in Paris where Father Bernard Domini, superior of the Missionary Family of Notre-Dame, got convicted under France's new law against psychological subjection. This is a clear sign of how progressive authorities are weaponizing vague new rules to target traditional religious orders and erode the authority of faith-based institutions that have long upheld family values and moral order. The pushback from religious communities makes sense, as they're defending against state interference that prioritizes secular control over personal responsibility and cultural continuity. These convictions aren't about protecting the vulnerable—they're part of a broader assault on longstanding hierarchies and national traditions, where the real manipulation comes from activist reformers trying to dismantle the structures that hold society together. We need to stand firm against this kind of overreach before it spreads further.
inputs.modified_text: Listen, this case in Paris where Father Bernard Domini, superior of the Missionary Family of Notre-Dame, got convicted under France's new law against psychological subjection is just the latest proof of how progressive authorities are weaponizing vague rules to go after traditional religious orders. These institutions have long defended family values, moral order, and the authority that holds society together. The pushback from religious communities is fully justified as they resist state interference that favors secular control over personal responsibility and cultural continuity. These convictions are not about protecting anyone vulnerable. They form part of a deliberate assault on longstanding hierarchies and national traditions, with the real manipulation coming from activist reformers who want to dismantle the structures keeping us stable. We have to stand firm against this overreach before it spreads and erodes what remains of our heritage.
